text.p: - Slovenian President Milan Kucan said the first session of the newly elected parliament will be held on November 28.
- Defence Minister Jelko Kacin said Slovenian troops may join an international force of the United Nations Organisation next year in Cyprus.

- Marjan Podobnik, head of the People's Party which belongs to the rightist "Spring Parties", invited Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek to talks about possible future cooperation between the parties. The "Spring Parties" got 45 out of 90 seats in the November 10 general election.
- River Drava in eastern Slovenia caused some flooding after recent heavy rain.
- Employees at newspaper Slovenec will continue to strike until they receive their salaries from the past few months.
- Slovenian trade unions, who demand that social benefits should remain unchanged, fail to attend negotiations with employers.
- Analysts say a coalition of rightist "Spring Parties" could harm Slovenia's market and bankers by its intention to revise some of the country's vast privatisation.
- Slovenia's only port Luka Koper debuts on the main section of Ljubljana's bourse on Wednesday.
